extraction_notes: Tsao et al. studied 13 Trifolium pratense cultivars and measured leaf, flower, petiole, and stem isoflavones using HPLC-DAD-MS. Their PubMed abstract confirms irilone among quantified minor aglycones. The exact 0.06 mg/g dry-weight leaf value was retrieved from American Herbal Pharmacopoeia Red Clover monograph (2017), Table 3, which attributes it to Tsao et al. 2006. Red clover leaves and flowers are documented as edible and used in salads, tea, or syrup by a separate 2023 primary food-context study (Mikulić et al., Foods 2024;13:103, doi:10.3390/foods13010103).
uncertainty_notes: This is a literature summary for red clover leaves, not a sample-specific observation. The underlying primary numerical table was not directly accessible in this review; the value is explicitly attributed to the primary study by a pharmacopoeial monograph. Original cultivar-level values, averaging rule, geography, and exact n for this summary are not available here. Dry-weight basis is retained; do not interpret as fresh-leaf concentration or supplement content.
